copy.title: Pitch deck: comps slide
copy.body: Last Dance is a time-loop dark comedy in the lane of Palm Springs, Ready or Not, Groundhog Day and Happy Death Day. Primary comps: Villains (fit 0.97, Niche, Top 6%) for tense, couple-in-a-bad-night comedy; The Kid Detective (fit 0.96, Niche, Top 5%) for a worn-down protagonist stuck in a small, sad professional world; Come to Daddy (fit 0.98, Niche, Top 8%) for the strongest overall affinity. Freaky (fit 0.94, Mid-list, Top 3%) shows the ceiling for a high-concept genre hook. All comps are 2019 or later, so the window is current. Audience skews ≤24 (+0.13) and 35–44 (+0.08), and female (0.23). Markets: Austin and Anchorage read as hidden gems; Los Angeles, Seattle, Miami and Las Vegas are emerging.

copy.title: Who it's for
copy.body: The audience over-indexes among viewers 24 and under (+0.13) and 35–44 (+0.08), and skews female (0.23 against male -0.23). Their taste descriptors run to murder, female protagonist, small town and detective stories, so they like a mystery under the comedy. The same group also likes Somebody Somewhere, Kevin Can F**k Himself and Forever on TV, and podcasts such as Welcome to Night Vale and My Dad Wrote A Porno. Austin and Anchorage show as hidden gems, which suggests room for local and festival-led outreach.

kit.headline: Palm Springs and Groundhog Day supply the loop, Ready or Not and Happy Death Day supply the dark edge, and Villains and The Kid Detective show indie buyers a recent audience for that mix.
kit.summary: Last Dance sits in the recent indie dark-comedy loop space, closest to Villains and The Kid Detective, both strong fits to the touchstones. The audience skews ≤24 (+0.13) and 35–44 (+0.08), and leans female. It under-indexes at 30–34 (-0.55). Lead with the loop and the grandmother's secret, then the bleak workplace humor. Affinity is aggregate taste, not a forecast.
